outcome: A multi-tenant backup service with per-tenant reporting and pricing that keeps pace with each tenant’s data growth.
overview: A managed service provider building a backup-as-a-service offering faces a different problem from an enterprise protecting itself: multi-tenancy, per-tenant reporting and delegated administration, and a cost model that has to survive a customer whose data grows faster than their contract expected. The Veeam Cloud Service Provider programme is built for exactly that shape, and here the buyer is the provider rather than the end customer. The commercial design — specifically how tenant data growth is passed through to tenant pricing — matters far more here than any technical choice on the platform, and it is where these services usually lose their margin.

benefits.text: Tenants are isolated with per-tenant reporting and delegated administration
benefits.limits: Isolation is logical within a shared platform; a tenant requiring physical separation needs a different design and a different price

benefits.text: Rental licensing aligns provider cost with tenant consumption rather than with committed capacity
benefits.limits: Alignment holds only if the provider’s own pricing passes growth through; a fixed tenant price against rental cost transfers the risk to the provider

benefits.text: Recovery services can be offered alongside backup as a differentiated tier
benefits.limits: Backup success rate is not recoverability; only a tested restore against a stated objective evidences it, and the two are routinely substituted for one another

residency: Provider-operated repositories in the provider’s chosen region, declared to tenants in the service description

notFor.situation: An enterprise protecting only its own estate
notFor.why: Multi-tenancy and rental licensing exist to serve a provider business model

notFor.situation: A provider without a defined service description and pricing model
notFor.why: The platform decision is downstream of the commercial design, not a substitute for it

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Veeam service provider partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a platform with the first tenants onboarded
Support model: Vendor rental support for the provider; Redington coordinates the vendor case and the licensing relationship.
1) Service design — pricing model, growth pass-through, service description and tenant objectives
2) Design — multi-tenant platform layout, isolation model, metering and repository growth plan
3) Build — platform deployed with metering and per-tenant reporting verified
4) Onboard and hand over — first tenants live with tested recovery, operations handed over
deliverables: Per-tenant reporting is produced without manual assembly
Metered consumption reconciles with rental licensing reporting
A tenant recovery completes within that tenant’s contracted objective
